- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ 0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 2–5% to account for downward momentum.
- If model shows a sharp spike followed by a steep drop (e.g., 30d forecast peaks then falls), reduce forecast by 10–15% in the following 5–7 days to avoid overshoot.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 30d price drops from 80+ to 70+), model often fails to adjust; apply a 5–10% downward bias in forecast if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- For 30d horizon, if model forecast is > 10% above recent 18d average, reduce by 5–10% unless sentiment is strongly bullish.
- If sentiment history shows a recent reversal (e.g., from + to -), model often lags; adjust forecast 1–3 days ahead to reflect sentiment shift.
- When sentiment is high but price is falling, model overreacts; reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid “sentiment-driven overcorrection.”
